say.text: A 58-year-old man has a groin sac found at laparoscopy. It comes through the posterior wall of the canal, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.
Which hernia is it? Answer from what you already remember.

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Set the name aside. Trace the sac: does it enter at the deep ring, or come through the posterior wall of the canal?
Yes. A direct hernia bulges through Hesselbach's triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.
So the side of the vessels decides the route. The name only tells you the family.

choices.label: I have it, skip the route lesson

say.text: Tempting: indirect is the commonest groin hernia, so it feels like the safe pick.
It fails on the route. An indirect sac enters at the deep ring, lateral to the vessels. This sac is medial to them.
Try again, and trace the route rather than the name.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check your reason: were you reading the name, or the route?

say.text: Tempting: a sac on the medial side of the groin feels like the femoral type, since both sit in the groin.
It fails on position. A femoral hernia lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. This one comes through the posterior wall of the canal.
Try again, and place the sac on the route first.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check where the femoral type sits against the pubic tubercle.

say.text: Names mislead here. 'Direct' and 'indirect' describe the route the sac takes, so read the route.
An indirect hernia enters at the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, and runs down the canal in the cord coverings.
A direct hernia bulges through Hesselbach's triangle, through the posterior wall, medial to the vessels.
Now the other groin type: a femoral hernia.
Where does its neck sit relative to the pubic tubercle?

choices.label: Above and medial to the tubercle
Below and lateral to the tubercle
Below and medial to the tubercle
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Use the pubic tubercle as the landmark. Is the femoral neck higher than the inguinal type, or lower?
Yes. A femoral hernia lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle.
An inguinal hernia emerges above and medial to it. That position is what separates the two.
Tempting: the inguinal position is the one you know best, so it gets copied onto the femoral type.
It fails on the tubercle. An inguinal hernia emerges above and medial to it. A femoral one lies below and lateral.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so the inguinal position may have been carried across. Check it against the tubercle.

say.text: Tempting: the femoral type sits on the medial side of the groin, so medial feels right.
It fails on the tubercle. The femoral neck lies lateral to it, and below. Medial is where the inguinal type sits.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the side of the tubercle before you trust 'medial'.

say.text: Put the two side by side against the same landmark, the pubic tubercle.
Inguinal: above and medial. Femoral: below and lateral. Hold that pair and the position settles the type.
An exam stem asks: most common hernia in females. Which do you pick?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Read the stem as a ranking. Which type leads overall, and does a female skew change that ranking?
Yes. Indirect inguinal hernia is the most common hernia overall, in both sexes and in children.
The female skew changes femoral's share, not the top of the ranking.
Tempting: femoral is the type you remember as female-skewed, so it feels like the female answer.
It fails on the qualifier. Femoral is relatively more common in women, but indirect still leads in women.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the word 'relatively' in the stem.

say.text: Tempting: direct is the other inguinal type you reach for, so it can look like a safe second pick.
It fails on the ranking. Indirect is the most common hernia in women as well as in men.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so a skew between sexes does not reorder the ranking.

say.text: 'Relatively more common in women' compares women with men. 'Most common in women' ranks the types within women.
Indirect inguinal hernia tops the ranking in women, as in men. The femoral skew does not move it.
Same idea, now as a statement. Which one is correct?

choices.label: Femoral hernia outnumbers every inguinal type in women
Femoral is relatively commoner in women, yet indirect leads
Direct hernia is the commonest type in women
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Keep two readings apart: a relative skew between the sexes, and a ranking inside one sex. Which statement keeps both true?
Yes. Femoral is relatively commoner in women, so the qualifier carries the meaning.
Indirect still tops the ranking in women, so the top spot does not move.
Tempting: a female skew sounds like it should lift femoral above every inguinal type.
It fails on the comparison. 'Relatively commoner' compares women with men. It is not a ranking, and indirect still leads in women.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check whether the statement ranks or compares.

say.text: Tempting: direct is a familiar inguinal type, so it can look like the female top pick.
It fails on the ranking. Indirect is the most common hernia in women, as the table gives it.
